mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine typically costs £650-£1,250 supply-only, depending on supplier and condition. Used units start from £550. Reconditioned units range £650-£1,000. Supply & fit adds £450-£900 labour. The 1.4 HDi is generally cheaper to replace than the 1.6 HDi.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi (8HZ) engine problems are head gasket failure causing coolant loss and white smoke, timing belt tensioner wear if service intervals are missed, and EGR valve sticking causing loss of power and rough idle. The 1.4 HDi is generally reliable but requires strict maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 207 1.4 HDi values typically £600-£1,800, a rebuilt engine at £650-£1,250 represents a significant investment. For sub-£1,000 examples, a used engine from £550 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi (8HZ) engine typically reaches 120,000-150,000 miles. Strict timing belt intervals (80,000 miles / 8 years), regular oil changes and coolant system maintenance are essential for longevity. The 1.4 HDi is generally durable when serviced correctly.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi and 1.6 HDi engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.4 HDi (8HZ) is a 1.4-litre 8-valve SOHC diesel producing 68-70hp, while the 1.6 HDi (9HX/9HZ) is a 1.6-litre 16-valve DOHC diesel producing 90-112hp. The 1.4 HDi is simpler, more economical (65+ mpg) and cheaper to replace, but less powerful and more prone to head gasket failure.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine code is 8HZ (DV4TD). It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block near the timing belt cover, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi (8HZ) was the entry-level diesel engine for the 207 range, offering exceptional fuel economy and low running costs for budget-conscious UK drivers. Part of PSA's DV4 engine family, the 1.4 HDi was fitted to Active, Access and Sport trims from launch in 2006 until 2012. Its simple 8-valve SOHC design and mechanical injection system made it reliable when maintained, but strict timing belt intervals and head gasket vulnerabilities remain key replacement drivers today.

milestones.description: **2006** - 207 launched with 1.4 HDi (8HZ) producing 68hp, paired with 5-speed manual gearbox
**2007** - SW estate variant introduced with same 1.4 HDi engine
**2008** - Power output increased to 70hp with minor ECU refinement
**2010** - Revised EGR valve calibration for emissions compliance
**2012** - 1.4 HDi phased out in favour of 1.6 HDi and PureTech petrol alternatives

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every 8HZ engine fitted to the Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi (8HZ) is generally a robust, economical diesel - but age, high mileage and the demands of the emissions system create distinct failure patterns. Head gasket failure, timing belt tensioner wear and EGR valve sticking are the most common drivers of replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Head Gasket Failure - Why Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi Engines Overheat and Lose Coolant
problems.rootCause: The aluminium block can warp under high thermal load, allowing the head gasket to fail. Symptoms include coolant loss, white smoke from the exhaust, mayonnaise in the oil cap and overheating. The 1.4 HDi is particularly susceptible if the cooling system has been neglected or if the engine has been run low on coolant.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Head Gasket & Cylinder Head Refurbishment
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head removal, pressure test, resurfacing, new MLS gasket, cooling system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; requires no further internal damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded head gasket, new timing belt, water pump and EGR valve
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating has caused bearing damage or piston scoring

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi is losing coolant without visible leaks, suspect head gasket failure immediately. A top-end refurbishment is cost-effective if caught early. However, if the engine has been overheated repeatedly or there is evidence of oil-water mixing, a full rebuilt 8HZ engine with a reinforced MLS gasket is the safest long-term solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 8HZ Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - Why Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi Engines Break Valves
problems.rootCause: The 1.4 HDi uses a timing belt that must be replaced at strict intervals - typically every 80,000 miles or 8 years. If the belt snaps, valves collide with pistons, causing catastrophic engine damage. Owners frequently miss the interval, leading to sudden failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New timing belt, tensioner, water pump and coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended at 80,000 miles or 8 years; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new timing belt, tensioner and water pump
repairOptions.longevity: Required if belt has snapped causing valve damage

problems.recommendation: Do not ignore the timing belt interval on your Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi. A £300-£500 preventative belt change is significantly cheaper than a £650-£1,250 engine replacement. If the belt has already snapped, a full rebuilt engine is the only option.
problems.cta: -> Find rebuilt 8HZ Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi engines with warranty

problems.h4: EGR Valve Failure - Why Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi Engines Lose Power
problems.rootCause: Carbon buildup from exhaust gases sticks the EGR valve open or closed, disrupting the air-fuel mixture and triggering fault codes. Owners report loss of power, rough idle, limp mode and increased fuel consumption. The 1.4 HDi's EGR is sensitive to short-journey driving patterns.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove valve, clean with solvent, reinstall and reset ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Works if valve mechanism isn't worn or seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply and fit new EGR valve, gaskets, recalibrate system
repairOptions.longevity: Restores function; may need intake manifold clean too

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new EGR valve and refreshed emissions system
repairOptions.longevity: Only needed if EGR failure has caused turbo or piston damage

problems.recommendation: EGR issues on the Peugeot 207 1.4 HDi are common but usually fixable without engine replacement. A £90-£220 specialist clean can restore function. Only consider a rebuilt engine if the fault has already caused turbo or internal wear. The 1.4 HDi's EGR valve is simpler than the 1.6 HDi's and generally cheaper to replace.
